scope: Complete source read; finite Brownian Gaussian/projective family, original Ionescu–Tulcea trajectory successor, measurable history gluing and actual conditional-kernel API read. Independent exact-source elaboration, signatures/axioms and duplicate/nonmonotone-time consumers executed.

semantic_review.finding: Public countableLaw takes only the requested time sequence. It uses actual finite Gaussian laws, splits each next finite prefix by the existing measurable append equivalence, takes its constructed condKernel and calls the original Kernel.trajMeasure. No Brownian process hB, projective-limit object or desired prefix-equality certificate is an input.

prefixRealization_law legitimately assumes normalized consistent finite laws as an internal helper. countableLaw_prefix instantiates it with finiteLaw_restrict, proved directly from BrownianReal.isProjectiveMeasureFamily_projectiveFamily. That is a source derivation, not the intended infinite conclusion hidden in a public field.

Finite Gaussian image laws are probability measures; initialLaw is the actual singleton-prefix evaluation, and the next split measure gives a total Markov conditional. Prefix equality follows from the original trajectory successor identity, conditional disintegration and inverse append reassembly. Null-prefix totalizations do not change the actual finite marginals.

finiteLaw first samples the finite IMAGE of requested physical times and selects its coordinates. Duplicate requests share one coordinate rather than independently sampling equal-law Gaussians. Consistency uses image subsets and commuting restriction maps, requiring no monotonicity or injectivity. The enumeration-index kernel is history-dependent and is not asserted to be a chronological Brownian semigroup.

countableLaw_finite covers every finite coordinate set by an Iic supremum prefix and proved restriction. Empty sets and repeated physical times are covered by the same types; there is no nonempty-set side condition.

finiteLaw_isGaussian uses the actual continuous linear coordinate-selection map of the original finite Gaussian law. countable_isGaussianProcess is then built from actual finite-law HasLaw proofs, not assumed Gaussian-process input. Coordinate/increment laws, zero mean, min-time covariance, variance and increment second moments are transported from those SAME laws.

denseTimes explicitly includes physical time0 at index0 and time1 at index1, with a proved dense tail. That exact sequence is supplied to countableLaw; dense_source_zero and dense_source_unit_variance concern the SAME actual measure. dense_source_realized is unconditional on any pre-existing Brownian source and has nonzero noise with deterministic zero start.

independent_edge_consumers: For arbitrary tau and indices k,l with tau k=tau l, the exact increment Gaussian law specializes to Dirac0, yielding omega k=omega l almost surely under countableLaw tau. This checks dependence at duplicate times.

A nonchronological sequence whose physical time at index0 is1 and later indices are0 has variance1 at coordinate0 by the actual general theorem. Thus neither chronological order nor zero starting physical time is silently required.
reuse_review: Uses existing BrownianReal.projectiveFamily/finite Gaussian map, probability, moment and projectivity theorems rather than postulating a new Gaussian family.
Uses existing DynamicsKernel appendHistory equivalence and original general Kernel.trajMeasure APIs; does not edit older countable-state wrappers or add another path-measure framework.
Uses constructed finite-measure condKernel and Measure.IsCondKernel.disintegrate; no caller-supplied IsCondKernel assumption appears in the public source.
limits: No all-nonnegative-real-time IsPreBrownianReal or IsBrownianReal is established; this countable-index Gaussian source alone does not discharge the existing OU hB premise.
Density and exact L2 increment control do not by themselves prove continuous sample paths. All-real coordinate completion and continuous modification remain separate required constructions.
No pathwise SDE identity, stochastic integral, general C2 Ito/localization, adapted HJB or Girsanov theorem is inferred.
The source is a noncomputable mathematical probability-law construction, not empirical evidence or a new registered sampling run; no old data/failure or random batch is changed.
Countable source success is a mandatory foundation dependency, not P11 or whole-theory closure.
